findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent builds of the same index key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its whole body, which serialized index creation. Now only the cache write is locked, so two callers for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a watch event handler plus startup build, or two concurrent search requests that both see a nil index via GetIndex) can run bleve.New() against the same on-disk directory concurrently. bleve.New fails or corrupts state when the directory already exists/is open, and the second winner overwrites the cache entry while the first index is still referenced by a caller. Some per-key coordination (e.g. a keyed mutex / singleflight) is needed, not just a cache-write lock.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads b.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no lock while BuildIndex now writes to the map under cacheMu from worker goroutines and from the watch-event path. Concurrent map read/write panics the process. This is newly reachable because search.init() now logs s.search.TotalDocs() and index builds can be triggered asynchronously by the watch goroutine. Take cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks the server context and background resources
findings.body: When s.Init(ctx) returns an error, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling cancel() on the context created above (and without stopping any lifecycle/blob resources already initialized). The context and any goroutines started during partial init (e.g. the storage watch poller started by backend WatchWriteEvents) are leaked for the life of the process. Call cancel() (and ideally s.Stop) before returning the error.

findings.title: Shared `err` variable written from concurrent errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Inside the `for _, info := range stats` loop, each goroutine assigns to the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and also increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed` counter without synchronization. With initWorkers > 1 these are concurrent writes to the same variables — a data race that can be detected by -race and can mask or mis-report build errors (one goroutine's error being overwritten by another's nil). Use a goroutine-local `err :=` and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Postgres path of the storage-server integration test is now skipped
findings.body: The only integration test exercising the storage server target is disabled for postgres with a TODO. Since this PR changes initialization to happen eagerly at ResourceServer construction (the riskiest behavioral change here), the test that would catch startup regressions no longer runs on postgres in CI, leaving that configuration uncovered.
